close_reason: Changed ClosureHandler.{backend, call_fn} from pub to pub(crate). All workspace consumers already use ::new() — no migration needed. Workspace cargo test and clippy pass.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:383-405 — ClosureHandler is #[non_exhaustive] with a constructor new(), but BOTH internal fields (backend: Arc<B>, call_fn: Box<...>) are pub. The #[non_exhaustive] attribute prevents external struct-literal construction but does NOT prevent field-by-field assignment after construction:

  let mut h: ClosureHandler<B, C> = ClosureHandler::new(backend, call_fn);
  h.call_fn = some_other_closure;  // compiles fine

A caller can hot-swap the closure mid-flight (assuming exclusive ownership, which Arc<ClosureHandler> precludes — but the type is consumed by-value in Arc::new before being shared, so the window is narrow but real). More to the point, the pub-field surface invites readers to think field-by-field mutation is intended.

Maintenance consequence: a future contributor writes code that uses h.call_fn = ... or h.backend = some_replacement, treating ClosureHandler as a struct-of-parts rather than an opaque handle. When the constructor gains a new derived field (e.g. a registered method name for tracing), their mutation pattern breaks invariants the constructor enforces.

Recommendation: make both fields pub(crate) or private with getters if external read access is needed. The constructor remains the only construction path. Update doc to clarify the type is an opaque handle.

If the public fields are intentional for some downstream consumer pattern, document the invariant the consumer must maintain. Currently nothing documents them as public for any reason.
title: ClosureHandler exposes pub fields that invite hot-swap footgun
